symptoms.symptom: Top burners do not light or do not burn evenly. (The front right burner is designed to have slightly smaller flames between the 6 and 9 o’clock positions. This is normal.)

causes.label: Plug on range is not completely inserted in the electrical outlet.
remedies: Make sure electrical plug is plugged into a live, properly grounded outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Plug on range is not completely inserted in the electrical outlet."

causes.label: Burner slits on the side of the burner may be clogged.
remedies: Remove the burner heads and clean them.
Check the electrode area for burned-on food or grease.
See the Care and cleaning of the range section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Burner slits on the side of the burner may be clogged."

causes.label: Improper burner assembly.
remedies: Make sure the burner parts are installed correctly.
See the Care and cleaning of the range section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Improper burner assembly."

symptoms.symptom: Burner flames very large or yellow

causes.label: Improper air to gas ratio.
remedies: If range is connected to LP gas, contact the person who installed your range or made the conversion.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Improper air to gas ratio."

symptoms.symptom: Surface burners light but oven does not

causes.label: The oven gas shut-off valve may have accidentally been moved during cleaning or moving.
remedies: To check the oven gas shut-off valve, remove the drawer (see the Care and cleaning of the range section).
Remove the rear access panel by unscrewing the thumb screws in the upper left and right corner.
Look for the gas shut-off lever at the back of the range.
Lever is shown closed.
Thumb screws PULL TO OPEN.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "The oven gas shut-off valve may have accidentally been moved during cleaning or moving."

symptoms.symptom: Scratches (may appear as cracks) on cooktop glass surface

causes.label: Incorrect cleaning methods being used.
remedies: Scratches are not removable.
Tiny scratches will become            Installation less visible in time as a result of cleaning.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Incorrect cleaning methods being used."

causes.label: Cookware with rough bottoms being used or coarse particles (salt or sand) were between the cookware and the surface of the cooktop.
remedies: To avoid scratches, use the recommended cleaning procedures.
Make sure bottoms of cookware are clean before use, and use cookware with smooth bottoms.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Cookware with rough bottoms being used or coarse particles (salt or sand) were between the cookware and the surface of the cooktop."

causes.label: Cookware has been slid across the cooktop surface.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Cookware has been slid across the cooktop surface."

symptoms.symptom: Areas of discoloration on the glass cooktop surface

causes.label: Food spillovers not cleaned before next use.
remedies: See the Cleaning the glass cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Food spillovers not cleaned before next use."

causes.label: Hot surface on a model with a light colored glass cooktop.
remedies: This is normal.
The cooking zones may change color when hot or cooling down.
This is temporary and will disappear as the glass cools to room temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Hot surface on a model with a light colored glass cooktop."

symptoms.symptom: Plastic melted to the glass cooktop surface

causes.label: Hot cooktop came into contact with plastic placed on the hot cooktop.
remedies: See the Glass surface—Potential for permanent damage Section in the Cleaning the glass surface section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Hot cooktop came into contact with plastic placed on the hot cooktop."

symptoms.symptom: Pitting (or indentation) of the cooktop

causes.label: Hot sugar mixture spilled on the cooktop.
remedies: Call a qualified technician for replacement.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Hot sugar mixture spilled on the cooktop."

symptoms.symptom: Control signals after entering cooking time or start time Operating Food does not bake or roast properly in the upper oven

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.

causes.label: Shelf position is incorrect.
remedies: See the Using the upper oven section.

causes.label: Incorrect cookware or cookware of improper size being used.
remedies: See the Using the upper oven section.

causes.label: Oven thermostat needs adjustment.

causes.label: Clock not set correctly.
remedies: See the Using the clock and timer section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Clock not set correctly."

causes.label: Aluminum foil used improperly in the oven.
remedies: See the Care and cleaning of the range section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Aluminum foil used improperly in the oven."

causes.label: Oven bottom not securely seated in position.
remedies: See the Installation of the range section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Oven bottom not securely seated in position."

symptoms.symptom: Food does not broil properly in the upper oven

causes.label: Oven door not closed.
remedies: See the Using the upper oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Oven door not closed."

causes.label: Improper shelf position being used.
remedies: See the Broiling Guide.

causes.label: Food being cooked in a hot pan.
remedies: For best results, use a pan designed for broiling.

causes.label: Cookware not suited for broiling.
remedies: For best results, use a pan designed for broiling.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Cookware not suited for broiling."

causes.label: Oven bottom not securely seated in position.
remedies: See the Installation of the range section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Oven bottom not securely seated in position."

symptoms.symptom: Upper oven temperature too hot or too cold

causes.label: Oven thermostat needs adjustment.
remedies: See the Adjust the upper oven thermostat— Do it yourself! section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Oven thermostat needs adjustment."

symptoms.symptom: Clock and timer do not work

causes.label: Plug on range is not completely inserted in the electrical outlet.
remedies: Make sure electrical plug is plugged into a live, properly grounded outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Plug on range is not completely inserted in the electrical outlet."

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.
remedies: See the Using the clock and timer section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Oven controls improperly set."

symptoms.symptom: Upper oven light does not work

causes.label: Light bulb is loose or defective.
remedies: Tighten or replace the bulb.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "Light bulb is loose or defective."

causes.label: Plug on range is not completely inserted in the electrical outlet.
remedies: Make sure electrical plug is plugged into a live, properly grounded outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "Plug on range is not completely inserted in the electrical outlet."

symptoms.symptom: “Crackling” or “popping” sound

causes.label: This is the sound of the metal heating and cooling during both the cooking and cleaning functions.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "This is the sound of the metal heating and cooling during both the cooking and cleaning functions."

symptoms.symptom: Excessive smoking

causes.label: Excessive soil.
remedies: Touch the Clear/Off pad.
Open the windows to rid the room of smoke.
Wait until the LOCKED DOOR light goes off.
Wipe up the excess soil and reset the clean cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "Excessive soil."

symptoms.symptom: Oven door will not open after a clean cycle

causes.label: Oven too hot.
remedies: Allow the oven to cool below locking temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "Oven too hot."

symptoms.symptom: Oven not clean after a clean cycle

causes.label: Oven controls not properly set.
remedies: See the Using the self-cleaning upper oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "Oven controls not properly set."

causes.label: Oven was heavily soiled.
remedies: Clean up heavy spillovers before starting the clean cycle.
Heavily soiled ovens may need to self-clean again or for a longer period of time.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "Oven was heavily soiled."

symptoms.symptom: “LOCK DOOR” flashes in the display

causes.label: The self-clean cycle has been selected but the door is not closed.
remedies: Close the oven door.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "The self-clean cycle has been selected but the door is not closed."

symptoms.symptom: LOCKED DOOR light is on when you want to cook

causes.label: The oven door is locked because the temperature inside the oven has not dropped below the locking temperature.
remedies: Touch the Clear/Off pad.
Allow the oven to cool.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "The oven door is locked because the temperature inside the oven has not dropped below the locking temperature."

symptoms.symptom: “F—and a number or letter” flash in the display

causes.label: You have a function error code.
remedies: Touch the Clear/Off pad.
Allow the oven to cool for one hour.
Put the oven back into operation.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "You have a function error code."

causes.label: If the function code repeats.
remedies: Disconnect all power to the range for 5 minutes and then reconnect power.
If the function error code repeats, call for service.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 53: "If the function code repeats."

symptoms.symptom: Display goes blank

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

symptoms.symptom: Operating

causes.label: The clock is in the black-out mode.
remedies: See the Special features of your oven control section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "The clock is in the black-out mode."

symptoms.symptom: Display flashes

causes.label: Power failure.
remedies: Reset the clock.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "Power failure."

symptoms.symptom: Unable to get the display to show “SF”

causes.label: Oven control pads were not pressed properly.
remedies: The Bake and Broil Hi/Lo pads must be touched at the same time and held for 3 seconds.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "Oven control pads were not pressed properly."

symptoms.symptom: Power outage, clock flashes

causes.label: Power outage or surge.
remedies: Reset the clock.
If the oven was in use, you must reset it by touching the Clear/Off pad, setting the clock and resetting any cooking function.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "Power outage or surge."

symptoms.symptom: “Burning” or “oily” odor emitting from the vent

causes.label: This is normal in a new oven and will disappear in time.
remedies: To speed the process, set a self-clean cycle for a minimum of 3 hours.
See the Using the self-cleaning oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "This is normal in a new oven and will disappear in time."

symptoms.symptom: Strong odor

causes.label: An odor from the insulation around the inside of the oven is normal for the first few times the oven is used.
remedies: This is temporary.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "An odor from the insulation around the inside of the oven is normal for the first few times the oven is used."

symptoms.symptom: Convection fan not working (some models)

causes.label: Preheat temperature not reached.
remedies: Fan will start automatically once the preheat temperature is reached.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "Preheat temperature not reached."

symptoms.symptom: Lower oven drawer will not work

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: The oven is self-cleaning.
remedies: Wait for the self-clean cycle to finish and the oven to cool.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "The oven is self-cleaning."

causes.label: Controls improperly set.
remedies: See the Lower oven drawer section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "Controls improperly set."

symptoms.symptom: Excessive condensation in the lower oven drawer

remedies: Remove liquid.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "Liquid in lower oven drawer."

causes.label: Uncovered foods.
remedies: Cover food with lid or aluminum foil.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 54: "Uncovered foods."

causes.label: Temperature setting too high.
remedies: Reduce temperature setting.
